usage: This is the standard formal way to say goodbye in Modern Standard Arabic, used in news broadcasts, formal speeches, and literature. It is universally understood across the Arab world but rarely used in casual street conversation where local dialects prevail. It carries a polite tone suitable for addressing anyone regardless of age, gender, or status.

variants.label: with safety
variants.note: A very common alternative that is widely used in both MSA and regional dialects.

variants.label: in God's protection
variants.note: Used to wish someone safety upon their departure, often carrying a sincere or slightly religious tone.

variants.label: farewell
variants.note: A highly formal and dramatic way to say goodbye, often implying a long or permanent separation.

examples.english: Thank you for your attendance, and goodbye.
Goodbye, see you tomorrow at school.

examples.arabic: سَأُغَادِرُ الآنَ، إِلَى اللِّقَاءِ يَا أَصْدِقَائِي.
examples.transliteration: sa'ughadiru al-'an, ila al-liqa' ya asdiqa'i.
examples.english: I will leave now, goodbye my friends.
